body.p: JALv3 extends the integer types beyond the 32-bit DWORD of JALv2 with 64-bit and 128-bit types. They are ordinary integer types: they can be used in expressions, arrays, records, procedure parameters, and as pointer pointee contracts.
The derivation rule of the smaller types still applies: QWORD is equivalent to BYTE*8, OWORD to BYTE*16, and the signed types add the SIGNED attribute to the same widths.
Literals may be written as decimal numbers (underscores are allowed as digit separators) or in hexadecimal with a 0x prefix. A leading minus sign makes a signed value.
body.codeblock: CONST QWORD GOLDEN = 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 VAR QWORD total = 0 VAR SQWORD delta = -1 VAR OWORD counter = 0 VAR SOWORD floor = -1
body.p: Arithmetic, shifts, bitwise operators, and comparisons operate on the full width of the value. When operands of different widths meet, the narrower value is promoted to the wider type, as with the smaller integer types.
body.codeblock: total = total + 0x1111111111111111 IF total > GOLDEN THEN total = total << 1 END IF
body.p: A wide value occupies contiguous bytes in data memory, least significant byte first. Byte overlays can be used to inspect or fill the individual bytes:
body.codeblock: VAR QWORD value VAR BYTE view[8] AT value VAR QWORD high AT big_value + 8
body.p: COUNT returns the storage width in bytes, so COUNT(total) is 8 and COUNT(counter) is 16. See for COUNT and the text conversion casts.
